itens.t: North Korean Leader Kim Jong Un Makes Surprise Visit to China to Mark Anniversary
itens.r: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un made an unannounced visit to Dandong, China, to mark the 76th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers' entry into the Korean War. The sudden cross-border trip caught local residents off guard and triggered tight security restrictions across the border region. Analysts note the visit underscores ongoing efforts to strengthen bilateral ties amid heightened regional tensions. The rare diplomatic outing highlights Pyongyang's reliance on Beijing as geopolitical friction on the peninsula intensifies.
itens.d:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un made a same-day visit to Dandong, China, to mark the 76th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers' entry into the Korean War. The brief visit was unusual for its commemorative purpose and the absence of a meeting with China's top leader.

Kim paid tribute at the Monument to Resisting America and Aiding Korea and toured the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea. The high-profile commemoration highlighted the historical solidarity and bilateral ties sealed in blood between the two countries.

itens.t: Exit Polls Show Deadlock in Israeli Election as Netanyahu Faces Strong Challenge
itens.r: Israel's first general election since October 7 ended in a parliamentary deadlock, according to exit polls showing neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rivals securing a clear majority. The high-stakes vote saw surging turnout and a historic surge for Arab-majority parties.
itens.d:
Israel's first election since October 7 appears deadlocked, according to exit polls. Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot is currently on track to secure a majority.

The political situation presents a strong challenge for Netanyahu as the electoral results remain extremely tight.

itens.t: SK hynix Reports Record Q3 Profit Amid Booming AI Chip Demand
itens.r: South Korea's SK hynix posted record-breaking third-quarter earnings driven by an ongoing supercycle in artificial intelligence memory chips. The chipmaker also announced massive shareholder return plans totaling tens of trillions of won.
itens.d:
SK hynix reported record third-quarter earnings and announced plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders this year. Booming demand for artificial intelligence memory pushed quarterly revenue above 100 trillion won for the first time.

The South Korean memory chip maker stated that its operating profit rose 38 percent from the previous quarter to 83.33 trillion won. This performance resulted in an operating margin of nearly 80 percent, alongside a 32 percent increase in revenue.

itens.t: Wall Street Closes Higher as Revived AI Momentum Lifts Tech Stocks
itens.r: U.S. equities finished the session higher, propelled by renewed investor enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence technologies. Major indices bounced back as optimism spread across semiconductor and software sectors.
itens.d:
Wall Street closed higher as revived momentum in artificial intelligence lifted technology stocks.

The positive market movement was driven by renewed enthusiasm for AI-related companies.

itens.t: Astronomers Discover Lava Exoplanet with Natural 'Sunscreen'
itens.r: Researchers observing the lava exoplanet TOI-561 b discovered that it reflects up to 75% of incoming stellar light without melting. The unusual planetary shield has puzzled astronomers studying extreme world atmospheres.
itens.d:
Researchers observed the lava exoplanet TOI-561 b for 37 hours across four orbits and found that it reflects about 75 percent of the starlight it receives without melting. Scientists believe this is made possible by a natural sunscreen of silicate mineral clouds that creates a barrier against radiation.

The science team used NASA's James Webb Space Telescope to monitor brightness and temperature variations as the exoplanet orbited its star. Observations revealed that the unilluminated side of the planet is cooler than expected for such a close rocky world.

itens.t: North Korea Deploys Self-Propelled Artillery Along Border with South Korea
itens.r: Pyongyang has deployed self-propelled artillery units along its western frontier as troops continue fortification efforts. The military movements come amid a backdrop of rising cross-border rhetoric and heightened alert levels.
itens.d:
North Korea has deployed self-propelled artillery pieces along its western border with South Korea. Troops have also continued fortification work along the frontier.

Photographs and videos captured at the Aegibong observatory in Gimpo confirmed at least three artillery pieces positioned on the northern side of the Jogang River.

itens.t: Nordic Leaders Urge Putin to End Ukraine War in Rare Direct Contact
itens.r: In an unusual direct diplomatic outreach, two Nordic leaders called directly on Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The dialogue marks a rare channel of communication between European heads of government and Moscow.
itens.d:
Two Nordic leaders urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring an end to the war in Ukraine. This development came through rare direct contact between European leaders and Putin.

The appeal highlights ongoing diplomatic efforts by Nordic nations regarding the conflict.

itens.d:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that his forces have recaptured territory from Russian troops. He emphasized that the Ukrainian military remains on the offensive.

The announcement highlights ongoing battlefield developments in the conflict.

itens.r: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro departed Brazil following his father's electoral defeat and subsequent legal scrutiny, securing a U.S. entry visa authorized by American officials. The departure drew sharp political criticism from domestic leaders in Brasilia.
itens.d:
Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil following an election loss, with the news arriving shortly after the US granted him an entry visa.

This development occurred just one day after Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passports during a money-laundering investigation.

itens.t: NASA Inspects Massive Sunshade for Upcoming NEO Surveyor Mission
itens.r: Engineers successfully inspected the 20-foot sunshade designed to protect NASA's upcoming Near-Earth Object Surveyor space telescope. The specialized shield is critical for keeping sensitive infrared instruments cool during asteroid-hunting operations.
itens.d:
A technician inspected the massive sunshade for NASA's Near-Earth Object Surveyor mission. The sunshade structure stands 20 feet tall and measures 8 feet wide at its base.

Designed to keep the infrared space telescope cool, the sunshade will assist the spacecraft in searching for near-Earth asteroids and comets while providing power. The mission will detect hard-to-find objects located in the direction of the Sun.

itens.t: UK Home Office Faces Potential Probe Over Use of OpenAI Technology

itens.d:
A government watchdog is considering a probe into the UK Home Office's use of ChatGPT technology. The tool has been utilized to process asylum claims.

The potential investigation stems from concerns regarding the accuracy of the artificial intelligence tools and the secrecy surrounding their deployment.

itens.t: Estudiantes President Dismisses Flamengo's Legal Challenge Over Copa Libertadores
itens.r: Estudiantes President Juan Sebastián Verón dismissed Flamengo's legal efforts to secure a berth in the Copa Libertadores final through administrative appeals. Verón insisted there is no risk to the scheduled tournament lineup.
itens.d:
Estudiantes president Juan Sebastián Verón addressed Flamengo's legal challenge regarding a Copa Libertadores roster spot tied to defender Rojo. Rojo required Court of Arbitration for Sport authorization to be registered after the Argentine transfer window closed.

Verón stated that Estudiantes sought proper legal counsel and that the CAS ruled in their favor. He added that the club faces no risk of missing the final and expressed eager anticipation for the match.

itens.t: Swiss Foreign Minister to Visit North Korea to Open Official Political Office
itens.r: Switzerland's foreign minister is scheduled to travel to Pyongyang to inaugurate the country's first dedicated political office. The diplomatic mission represents one of the highest-level visits by a Western official to North Korea in years.
itens.d:
Switzerland's foreign minister will travel to North Korea to attend the official opening of the first dedicated Swiss political office in Pyongyang. The event marks the highest-level visit by a Western official in years.

Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis will undertake a two-day visit beginning Thursday to meet with North Korean officials.

itens.t: Inca Study Reveals Breast Cancer Mortality Rate Is Nearly Four Times Higher in Black Women
itens.r: A comprehensive study released by Brazil's National Cancer Institute (Inca) showed that breast cancer mortality is nearly four times higher among Black women compared to white women. Public health advocates pointed to disparities in early diagnosis and treatment access.
itens.d:
A study by the Brazilian National Cancer Institute revealed that breast cancer mortality is nearly 3.8 times higher among Black women compared to white women in Brazil. The research compiled data from 24 studies across six countries over a 20-year period.

Although overall incidence is lower among Black women, they are more frequently affected by aggressive tumors like the triple-negative subtype and face diagnosis at younger ages and more advanced stages.

itens.t: Star Trek Legend Walter Koenig Passes Away at Age 90
itens.r: Actor Walter Koenig, beloved for his iconic portrayal of Pavel Chekov in the original 'Star Trek' television and film series, passed away at his home at age 90. Tributes poured in from science fiction fans and co-stars across the globe.
itens.d:
Actor Walter Koenig passed away at the age of 90 in his North Hollywood home. He was best known for portraying navigator Pavel Chekov in Star Trek.

Koenig played the role across two seasons of the original television series and in the first seven Paramount feature films. Born in Chicago, he later studied at the Neighborhood Playhouse School of the Theatre and built a celebrated career in television and film.

itens.t: São Paulo Police to Integrate Smart Sampa Data into Organized Crime Probes
itens.r: The city of São Paulo signed cooperative agreements allowing state prosecutors to leverage technical data from the Smart Sampa surveillance network. The initiative aims to enhance intelligence-led operations against organized crime rings.
itens.d:
The municipality of São Paulo signed agreements with the state public ministry to allow the Gaeco organized crime task force to use Smart Sampa technical data for investigations. The initiative aims to enhance public security technology integration.

Under the plan, Smart Sampa will issue alerts to the civil guard upon identifying registered individuals, while the public ministry provides a database. The system is also slated for independent technical review following a prior data leak.

itens.t: European Transport Strikes Threaten Travel Disruptions in Spain and Italy
itens.r: Upcoming transportation strikes by rail and aviation workers in Spain and Italy threaten widespread travel delays and cancellations for international passengers. Unions have called for walkouts to protest working conditions and wage disputes.
itens.d:
Travelers in Spain and Italy face major transportation disruptions due to upcoming strikes. Spanish train passengers could experience delays and cancellations starting Thursday, while a nationwide Italian strike on Friday will affect trains and flights.

In Spain, train drivers represented by the SEMAF union planned a 24-hour strike over concerns regarding railway safety and working conditions. The government mandated minimum service requirements for high-speed, long-distance, and medium-distance routes.

itens.t: NASA Remembers 1961 Saturn I Test Flight That Paved the Way for Moon Landings
itens.r: Space historians marked the anniversary of NASA's first successful Saturn I rocket test flight from Florida in 1961. The heavy-lift vehicle laid crucial engineering groundwork for the legendary Saturn V moon missions.
itens.d:
NASA launched the first test flight of the Saturn I space launch vehicle on October 27, 1961. The rocket was the United States' first heavy-lift vehicle designed to launch large payloads beyond low Earth orbit.

The liquid-powered rocket reached an altitude of 85 miles before splashing down in the Atlantic Ocean fifteen minutes later. Despite an early engine cutoff caused by an imbalance of liquid oxygen and propellant, the test paved the way for the Saturn V and future moon landings.

itens.t: Russian Court Jails IT Worker for 13 Years Over Cryptocurrency Donations to Ukraine
itens.r: A Russian court sentenced an information technology specialist to 13 years in prison after cryptocurrency exchange data linked him to financial contributions sent to Ukraine. The conviction highlights sweeping crackdowns on wartime dissent and digital financial flows.
itens.d:
A Russian court sentenced an IT worker to 13 years in prison over cryptocurrency donations made to Ukraine. The conviction followed data sharing from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange.

Binance provided Ukraine donation information directly to Russian authorities, leading to the severe sentence.

itens.t: South Korea Launches Large-Scale IT Infrastructure Inspections Following Cyberattacks
itens.r: The South Korean government announced sweeping vulnerability inspections across approximately 170 key private-sector IT infrastructures. The security audit comes in response to a string of recent cyberattacks targeting domestic institutions.
itens.d:
South Korea's science ministry will conduct large-scale security vulnerability inspections on approximately 170 key private sector IT infrastructures. The move follows recent cybersecurity breaches at public institutions and financial firms.

The assessments will target 111 public organizations managing vital internet-connected infrastructures and servers, with inspections concluding by the end of the year. President Lee Jae Myung has urged the development of AI-era cybersecurity methods following attacks on 16 commercial banks.

itens.d:
Shu Bao, the youngest giant panda born at Everland theme park in South Korea, will make her public debut at Panda World. The female cub was born to mother Ai Bao and father Le Bao through natural breeding.

Weighing just 171 grams at birth, the cub has grown to over 9 kilograms ahead of her first public appearance.

itens.d:

itens.r: Atlanta Dream head coach Karl Smesko and star player Angel Reese publicly criticized refereeing decisions following a contentious conclusion to the WNBA Finals. Critics argued that missed physical contact heavily influenced the series outcome.
itens.d:
Atlanta Dream head coach Karl Smesko criticized officiating after his team's Game 5 loss in the WNBA Finals. He argued that officials missed a ridiculous amount of contact against forward Angel Reese.

Reese recorded seven points and 15 rebounds in the 64-55 defeat to the Golden State Valkyries. Both Smesko and Reese expressed frustration regarding physical play and questionable referee decisions throughout the series.

itens.t: Brazilian Customs Seizes Over 17 Tons of Shark Fins Hidden in Export Container
itens.r: Federal tax authorities in Santa Catarina intercepted more than 17 tons of illegal shark fins packed inside a shipping container bound for international markets. The seizure highlights ongoing illicit wildlife trafficking networks operating through Brazilian ports.
itens.d:
Brazilian customs authorities seized over 17 tons of shark fins hidden inside an export container at the Port of Itapoá in Santa Catarina. The cargo was falsely labeled as frozen sardines and bound for Malaysia.

The illicit shipment was discovered through intelligence and monitoring by federal revenue agents. The material was transferred to Ibama for technical analysis and potential environmental infractions.

itens.t: Cowboy Space Unveils 'Big Iron' Rocket to Support AI Data Centers

itens.d:
Cowboy Space unveiled its Big Iron rocket system during an event in Palo Alto, California. The company, led by Baiju Bhatt, plans to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit.

The stainless-steel rocket features a reusable first stage and an upper stage that converts into a data-center satellite once in orbit. Powered by Clydesdale methalox engines, the vehicle utilizes a design configuration similar to SpaceX rockets.

itens.d: Volunteer networks across the United States mobilized to monitor polling places on Election Day. Volunteers prepared heat maps, Signal chats, and war rooms to address potential actions by federal immigration agents.

The match lasted one hour and twelve minutes, marking Williams' return to singles play since the US Open. She has not won a singles match since July 2025.
